research_question: How did Bartolomeo Cristofori invent the piano?

sources.title: The Piano: The Pianofortes of Bartolomeo Cristofori (1655–1731)
sources.reliability: Museum research essay by Wendy Powers
notes: Cristofori developed a hammer-action keyboard instrument around 1700, allowing players to control loudness by touch unlike the harpsichord.

sources.title: Grand Piano, Bartolomeo Cristofori, 1720
notes: The 1720 instrument is among the oldest surviving pianos and has 54 keys, showing how early pianos differed from modern instruments.

sources.title: Grand Piano
sources.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, MetKids
notes: The piano's name derives from pianoforte, referring to the ability to play soft and loud; its invention built on existing keyboard and string technologies.
